title: The State, the Government, and You

learn.hook: Governments come and go after elections, but India stays India. That's because the State and the government are not the same thing!
points: A State (country) has four elements: a defined territory, a population, a government and sovereignty (the power to make its own decisions without outside control).
The government is the group of people and institutions that run the State: they make laws, carry them out and settle disputes.
Governments change, for example after elections, but the State continues. India the State has existed since independence while many different governments have come and gone.
India is a democracy, because citizens elect their representatives, and a republic, because its head of state, the President, is elected and does not inherit the post.
In everyday speech, 'state' can also mean a part of India, like Kerala or Punjab. In this chapter, 'State' with a capital S means the whole country.

example.q: After a general election, a new party forms the government in New Delhi. Has the Indian State changed?
steps: The territory, the people and India's sovereignty are the same.
Only the people running the government have changed.
The government is one part of the State; it can change while the State continues.
example.answer: No. The government has changed, but the State of India continues.

learn.reallife: Your school stays the same even when a new principal takes charge, just as the State stays the same when a new government takes office.

games.title: Element of a State?
buckets: One of the four elements of a State

games.title: State or government?
items: A government can change after an election.
New representatives can form a new government.
The State of India ends whenever a new government is formed.
The State continues; only the government changes.
Sovereignty means a country makes its own decisions.
A sovereign State is free from outside control.
India is a republic because its head of state is elected.
The President of India is elected, not hereditary.
The government is just another name for the territory.
The government runs the State; territory is the land.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four elements of a State?
quiz.explain: The four elements are territory, population, government and sovereignty.
steps: The four elements of a State are territory, population, government and sovereignty.
A national airline is not one of them.
A country may have one, but does not need it to be a State.
Answer: A national airline
quiz.mistake: Adds things a country may have but does not need

quiz.q: Sovereignty means:
options: The power to make one's own decisions without outside control
quiz.explain: A sovereign State is independent in its internal and external affairs.
steps: A sovereign State makes its own decisions.
No outside power controls it.
So sovereignty means the power to make one's own decisions without outside control.
Answer: The power to make one's own decisions without outside control
quiz.mistake: Confuses sovereignty with military strength

quiz.q: What happens when a new government is elected?
options: The government changes but the State continues
quiz.explain: Only those who run the government change; the State remains.
steps: After an election, only the people running the government change.
The territory, population and sovereignty stay the same.
So the government changes but the State continues.
Answer: The government changes but the State continues
quiz.mistake: Thinks the State and the government are the same

quiz.q: Why is India a republic and not a monarchy?
options: Its head of state, the President, is elected
quiz.explain: In a republic, the head of state is chosen, not born into the post.
steps: In a republic, the head of state is elected, not born into the post.
India's head of state, the President, is elected.
So India is a republic.
Answer: Its head of state, the President, is elected
quiz.mistake: Confuses republic with democracy

quiz.q: The government is best described as:
options: The people and institutions that run the State
All the rivers of a country
quiz.explain: The government makes, carries out and interprets laws for the State.
steps: The government runs the State: it makes laws, carries them out and settles disputes.
It is not the land, rivers or flag.
So it is the people and institutions that run the State.
Answer: The people and institutions that run the State
quiz.mistake: Mixes up government with territory or symbols

quiz.q: India is a democracy because:
options: Its ruler is born into a royal family
Only a few people can vote
quiz.explain: In a democracy, people choose who governs them.
steps: In a democracy, people choose who governs them.
In India, citizens elect their representatives.
So India is a democracy.
Answer: Citizens elect their representatives
quiz.mistake: Confuses democracy with monarchy

quiz.q: In the phrase 'the State of India', the word State means:
quiz.explain: Here 'State' means the whole country, not a part of it.
steps: 'State' with a capital S here means the whole country.
A 'state' like Kerala is only a part of India.
So in 'the State of India' it means the whole country.
Answer: The whole country
quiz.mistake: Confuses the two meanings of 'state'

quiz.q: Which is an example of the government doing its work?
quiz.explain: Making laws is one of the main jobs of government.
steps: Making laws is a main job of government.
Floods, mountains forming and rain are natural events.
So Parliament passing a new law is the government at work.
Answer: Parliament passing a new law
quiz.mistake: Confuses natural events with government action

teach.ask: Gappu thinks the State and the government are the same thing. Explain the difference.
teach.praise: The State is the country with land, people, government and sovereignty; the government runs it and can change. Clear now!
teach.nudge: Good! What stays the same when a new government is elected?

revise.summary: A State has four elements: territory, population, government and sovereignty. The government runs the State and can change after elections while the State continues. India is a democracy and a republic.
focus: Name the four elements of a State
Tell the State from the government
Explain why India is a democracy and a republic
remember: Government: makes laws, carries them out, settles disputes
Democracy: citizens elect representatives; republic: elected head of state (the President)
traps: The State and the government are not the same thing
Sovereignty is independence, not just a big army
'State' with a capital S means the whole country, not a part like Kerala

topics.title: Three organs and three tiers of government

learn.hook: One group makes the rules, another carries them out, and a third settles arguments about them. That's how power is shared!
points: The government has three organs. The legislature makes laws; the executive carries out (implements) laws; the judiciary interprets laws and settles disputes.

At the national level, Parliament (the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha) is the legislature. The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers lead the executive. The Supreme Court, in New Delhi, is the highest court.
Keeping these organs separate, so that each checks the others, is called separation of powers. The judiciary in India is independent.
India has three tiers (levels) of government: the Union (central) government, State governments and local governments.

Local governments include panchayats in villages (gram panchayat, panchayat samiti and zila parishad) and municipalities and municipal corporations in towns and cities. The 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) gave them constitutional status.

example.q: A street light near your home is broken. Which tier of government should you ask to repair it?
steps: Street lights are a local matter.
In a town or city, the municipality or municipal corporation handles them; in a village, the gram panchayat.
So the local tier is the right level.
example.answer: The local government: the municipality, municipal corporation or gram panchayat.

learn.reallife: Your gram panchayat or municipal ward member, your MLA and your MP represent you at the three levels of government.

games.title: Tiers of government
games.prompt: From the largest area to the smallest

quiz.q: Which organ of government makes laws?
quiz.explain: The legislature, such as Parliament, makes laws.
steps: The three organs: legislature (makes laws), executive (carries them out), judiciary (interprets them).
So laws are made by the legislature.
Parliament is the legislature at the national level.
Answer: Legislature
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the jobs of the three organs

quiz.q: Which organ settles disputes and interprets laws?
quiz.explain: Courts interpret laws and decide disputes.
steps: The judiciary interprets laws and settles disputes.
The executive carries out laws; the legislature makes them.
So the answer is the judiciary.
Answer: Judiciary
quiz.mistake: Thinks the executive decides disputes

quiz.q: The executive at the Union level is led by:
options: The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
quiz.explain: The PM and ministers run the government and carry out laws.
steps: The executive carries out laws.
At the Union level it is led by the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
The Supreme Court is the judiciary; the Rajya Sabha is part of the legislature.
Answer: The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
quiz.mistake: Confuses the executive with the legislature or judiciary

quiz.q: India's Parliament consists of:
options: The Supreme Court and High Courts
The President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha
quiz.explain: Parliament has three parts: the President and the two Houses.
steps: Parliament is India's national legislature.
It consists of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
So all three together make Parliament.
Answer: The President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the President is part of Parliament

quiz.q: Keeping the three organs separate so that each can check the others is called:
quiz.explain: Separation of powers prevents any one organ from becoming too powerful.
steps: Keeping the legislature, executive and judiciary separate lets each check the others.
This is called separation of powers.
It stops any one organ from becoming too powerful.
Answer: Separation of powers
quiz.mistake: Does not know the term

quiz.q: What are the three tiers of government in India?
options: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and President
quiz.explain: Union, State and local governments work at different levels.
steps: India has three levels of government.
They are the Union (central), State and local governments.
Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and President are parts of Parliament, not tiers.
Answer: Union, State and local
quiz.mistake: Confuses tiers with organs

quiz.q: Which body is the lowest tier of the panchayati raj system?
quiz.explain: The gram panchayat works at the village level.
steps: Panchayati raj bodies: gram panchayat, panchayat samiti, zila parishad.
The gram panchayat works at the village level.
So it is the lowest tier.
Answer: Gram panchayat
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of panchayati raj bodies

quiz.q: Which amendments gave constitutional status to local governments?
quiz.explain: The 73rd (panchayats) and 74th (municipalities) Amendments were passed in 1992.
steps: Local governments got constitutional status in 1992.
This was done by the 73rd (panchayats) and 74th (municipalities) Amendments.
So the answer is the 73rd and 74th Amendments.
Answer: 73rd and 74th Amendments
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous amendments

teach.ask: Gappu asks how India's government is organised. Explain the three organs and the three tiers.
teach.praise: Lawmakers, law-runners and law-judges, at Union, State and local levels. Power is shared smartly!
teach.nudge: Good! Can you also tell me about the levels of government, from the Union to the village?

revise.summary: The government has three organs: the legislature makes laws, the executive carries them out and the judiciary interprets them, kept apart by separation of powers. India has three tiers: Union, State and local, with panchayats and municipalities given constitutional status in 1992.
focus: Name the three organs and their jobs
Know the Union legislature, executive and judiciary
Name the three tiers and the local bodies
remember: Legislature: makes laws; executive: carries them out; judiciary: interprets them
Parliament = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha; PM and Council of Ministers lead the executive
Panchayati raj: gram panchayat, panchayat samiti, zila parishad; 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992)
traps: Don't confuse organs (legislature, executive, judiciary) with tiers (Union, State, local)
Don't leave the President out of Parliament; the President is part of it
The gram panchayat is the lowest tier, not the zila parishad

topics.title: You and the government: a citizen's role

learn.hook: Democracy is not just about voting once in five years. Citizens can question, suggest, complain and help, every day!
points: Citizens take part in government by voting in elections at all three tiers, from panchayat to Parliament, once they are 18.
In villages, every adult voter is a member of the gram sabha and can discuss village plans and question the panchayat.
The Right to Information Act, 2005, lets citizens ask government offices for information about their work.
Citizens can approach courts if their rights are violated, and they pay taxes that fund schools, roads and hospitals.
Good citizens also follow laws, protect public property, keep their surroundings clean and respect the rights of others. Children can start by being informed and responsible.

example.q: A road in a village was supposed to be repaired, but nothing has happened. Name two ways villagers could act.
steps: They can raise the issue at the gram sabha meeting and ask the panchayat for answers.
They can use the Right to Information Act to ask how the money for the road was spent.
They can also contact their elected representatives.
example.answer: Raise it in the gram sabha and use the RTI Act (or contact their representatives).

learn.reallife: When your school holds a student council election or a cleanliness drive, you are practising the habits of an active citizen.

games.title: Is it an active citizen's action?

items.text: Citizens can vote from the age of ___.
The RTI Act was passed in ___.
Every adult voter in a village is a member of the gram ___.
Taxes help pay for schools, roads and ___.

quiz.q: Which law lets citizens ask government offices for information?
quiz.explain: The RTI Act, 2005, gives citizens the right to ask for information.
steps: Citizens can ask government offices for information about their work.
This right comes from the Right to Information Act, 2005.
The Consumer Protection Act is about consumers.
Answer: Right to Information Act, 2005
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with other laws

quiz.q: Who is a member of the gram sabha?
options: Every adult voter of the village
quiz.explain: All adult voters in the village are members of the gram sabha.
steps: The gram sabha is the village meeting.
Every adult voter of the village is a member.
It is not only the sarpanch or officers.
Answer: Every adult voter of the village
quiz.mistake: Thinks only elected leaders are members

quiz.q: Why do citizens pay taxes?
options: To fund public services like schools, roads and hospitals
quiz.explain: Taxes provide money for services that benefit everyone.
steps: Taxes are money citizens pay to the government.
This money funds schools, roads and hospitals.
So taxes fund public services that benefit everyone.
Answer: To fund public services like schools, roads and hospitals
quiz.mistake: Does not know what taxes are used for

quiz.q: What can a citizen do if their Fundamental Rights are violated?
quiz.explain: Courts protect citizens' rights.
steps: Courts protect citizens' rights.
If a Fundamental Right is violated, a citizen can approach the court.
So they can go to court.
Answer: Go to court
quiz.mistake: Does not know about the role of courts

quiz.q: Which of these shows responsible citizenship?
quiz.explain: Taking care of public property is a duty of every citizen.
steps: Good citizens follow laws and protect public property.
Damaging lights, littering and ignoring rules are irresponsible.
So protecting public property shows responsible citizenship.
Answer: Protecting public property
quiz.mistake: Does not link everyday actions with citizenship

quiz.q: Citizens vote in elections for:
options: All three tiers: local, State and Union
quiz.explain: Citizens elect representatives at panchayat or municipal, State and Union levels.
steps: Citizens aged 18 and above vote at every level.
They vote for panchayats or municipalities, State and Union governments.
So they vote for all three tiers.
Answer: All three tiers: local, State and Union
quiz.mistake: Thinks voting happens only for Parliament

quiz.q: How can a 12-year-old be an active citizen?
options: By voting in Lok Sabha elections
By staying informed, following rules and keeping surroundings clean
quiz.explain: Children cannot vote yet, but they can be informed and responsible.
steps: A 12-year-old cannot vote yet.
But children can be informed, follow rules and keep their surroundings clean.
That is how they can be active citizens.
Answer: By staying informed, following rules and keeping surroundings clean
quiz.mistake: Thinks only adults can be good citizens

quiz.q: Villagers want to know how money for a new well was spent. Which is the best step?
options: Write angry words on a wall
File an RTI application or ask in the gram sabha
quiz.explain: RTI and the gram sabha are ways citizens can hold the government accountable.
steps: Citizens can hold the government accountable.
They can file an RTI application or ask in the gram sabha.
Waiting silently or writing on walls does not help.
Answer: File an RTI application or ask in the gram sabha
quiz.mistake: Does not know the tools citizens have

teach.ask: Gappu asks: what can an ordinary person do in a democracy? Tell him a citizen's role.
teach.praise: Vote, ask questions, use RTI, follow laws and care for public things. Citizens are powerful!
teach.nudge: Good! Besides voting, how can a citizen ask the government questions?

revise.summary: Citizens take part in government by voting at all three tiers from age 18, joining the gram sabha, using the RTI Act, 2005, going to court and paying taxes. Good citizens also follow laws, protect public property and respect others.
focus: Explain how citizens take part in government
Know the gram sabha and the RTI Act
Describe responsible citizenship, including for children
remember: Vote at 18 for local, State and Union governments
Gram sabha: every adult voter of the village
RTI Act, 2005: citizens can ask government offices for information
Taxes fund schools, roads and hospitals
traps: Voting is not only for Parliament
The gram sabha is not only the sarpanch
Children can't vote, but they can still be good citizens
